introduction: USDA Choice Angus Beef Boneless Bottom Round Roast Experience the rich, full flavor of Member's Mark USDA Choice Angus Beef Boneless Bottom Round Roast, priced per pound, a versatile and value-packed cut of beef. Whether you're preparing a hearty pot roast or a savory beef stew, this cut is sure to impress with 24g of protein per serving. Creative Ways to Prepare Your Roast Elevate your cooking with this bottom round roast by seasoning it with your favorite spices and pairing it with root vegetables like celery, onions, carrots, garlic, and potatoes. Slow cook overnight or for 6-8 hours on high for a melt-in-your-mouth pot roast. For a comforting beef stew, add cream of mushroom soup and beef stock, then serve over noodles. Alternatively, cook in a Dutch oven and use the drippings to create a flavorful gravy. Cooking Instructions 1. Thaw & Prep: Fully thaw the roast in the refrigerator. Pat dry and season generously with salt, pepper, and desired herbs. 2. Choose Cooking Method: For Slices (Roasting): Sear all sides in a hot pan (optional, but recommended). Place in a roasting pan in a 300°F-325°F oven. Cook for 20-25 mins per pound until desired internal temperature is reached. For Shredding (Braising/Pot Roast): Sear all sides in a Dutch oven. Add liquid (broth/water) to half-cover the roast, plus optional vegetables/herbs. Cover and bake in a 300°F-325°F oven for 3-4 hours until fork-tender. 3. Verify Doneness: Use a meat thermometer. For slicing, aim for 130-145°F (54-63°C) for medium-rare to medium-well. For shredded, ensure it's very tender. 4. Rest: Remove from heat, tent loosely with foil, and let rest for 15-20 minutes before slicing against the grain or shredding. Lemon-Marinated Rack of Lamb Recipe This recipe for rack of lamb takes a little more time to put together but is absolutely worth it. The lemon, garlic and fresh herb marinade is easy, just toss it together and let the flavor sink in. Top with a lemony panko crust then roast all-in-one on a sheet pan with potatoes. Ingredients ½ cup lemon juice ¼ cup olive oil 4 cloves garlic, chopped ½ cup chopped fresh flat leaf parsley 2 tablespoons chopped fresh rosemary leaves 2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano leaves 2 racks of lamb (8 ribs each) ½ cup plain panko 1 tablespoon grated lemon zest 1 ¼ pounds baby Yukon Gold potatoes, cut in half (or in 1-inch pieces, if large) Directions Pour the lemon juice into a glass bowl. Stir in half the following: oil, garlic and herbs. Remove and reserve 2 tablespoons lemon juice mixture for the potatoes. Season the lamb with salt and pepper. Add the lamb to the remaining lemon mixture. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 30 minutes or overnight. Remove the lamb from the lemon juice mixture and pat dry (discard remaining mixture) . Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir the remaining oil, garlic, herbs and the panko and lemon zest in another small bowl. Place the lamb, fat-side up, onto a rimmed baking sheet. Press the panko mixture onto the fat sides of the lamb. Toss the potatoes with the reserved lemon juice mixture and arrange on the baking sheet around the lamb. Roast for 25 minutes or until the internal temperature of the lamb reaches 135°F for medium (for best results, cover and let the lamb stand for 10 minutes before slicing). Note: It takes about 2 large lemons to yield ½ cup of lemon juice (to save time, you can also use store-bought bottled lemon juice). If you have an extra lemon, you can slice it to roast on the baking sheet with the lamb and potatoes- the roasted slices add a pop of bright flavor to your plate! Preparation for Boneless Leg of Lamb Roast at 350°F for approximately 18 minutes per pound. Using a thermometer cook to an internal temperature of 135°F to 140°F for medium doneness. Cooking Guide: Medium-Rare: 130-135°F internal temperature Medium: 135-140°F internal temperature Well-Done: 155-160°F internal temperature Recipe: Rosemary Boneless Leg of Lamb with Red Wine and Roasted Garlic Fig Sauce Imagine your house filled with the scent of roast lamb and rosemary while you entertain family and friends on a chilly winter holiday. You can prep this easy recipe in just 15 minutes, then relax and sip some red wine while it roasts to perfection. Add more red wine to the pan drippings, along with roasted garlic and figs for a pan sauce that's rich and savory and a little sweet, perfect for serving with the bold flavor of roasted leg of lamb. This Rosemary Leg of Lamb with Red Wine, Roasted Garlic and Fig looks and tastes amazing and will be an impressive centerpiece of your holiday table. Grab some Member’s Mark Aluminum Steam Pans for easy cleanup! Ingredients: 4 garlic cloves, minced ¼ cup chopped fresh rosemary ¼ cup olive oil 1 tablespoon kosher salt 1 teaspoon cracked black pepper 1 boneless leg of lamb (about 5 ½ pounds) (netting removed) 2 cups beef or veal stock 1 cup dry red wine 1 tablespoon tomato paste 2 sprigs fresh rosemary ¾ cup diced dried figs ½ cup mashed roasted garlic (mash store-bought roasted garlic or follow the tip below) ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley Directions: Mix the minced garlic, chopped rosemary, oil, salt and pepper in a glass measuring cup. Place the lamb into a 2.5 gallon-size (jumbo) resealable plastic bag or shallow baking dish. Brush the lamb with the garlic mixture. Seal the bag or cover the dish and refrigerate for 1 hour. Place the oven rack in the bottom third of your oven. Pour 1 cup water into the bottom of a roasting pan. Remove the lamb from the marinade and place on a rack in the roasting pan (discard the marinade) . SEAR at 450°F. for 20 minutes, then ROAST at 325°F. for 1 hour or until the internal temperature reaches 130-135°F (check the temperature after 30 minutes) for medium-rare (or until desired doneness). Remove the lamb to a cutting board, cover with foil and let stand for at least 15 minutes before slicing (lamb will continue cooking while it rests). Reserve the pan drippings and spoon off any fat. Heat the stock, wine, tomato paste and rosemary sprigs, figs and ½ cup reserved pan drippings in a 3-quart saucepan over high heat to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium. Cook for 15 minutes until the mixture is reduced by half. Stir in the roasted garlic and parsley and serve the sauce with the lamb. Meal Idea - Garlic Butter Bone-In Pork Chops Ingredients 4 Member's Mark Bone-In Assorted Pork Chops Salt and pepper to taste 2 tbsp olive oil 4 cloves garlic, minced 4 tablespoons unsalted butter Fresh herbs for garnish (such as rosemary, thyme, or parsley) Directions 1. Move the pork chops to one side of the skillet. On the other side, add minced garlic and butter. Stir the garlic in the butter and cook for about 1 minute until it becomes fragrant. 7. Spoon the garlic butter over the pork chops, making sure each one is well-coated. 8. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for about 10–15 minutes, or until the pork chops reach an internal temperature of 145°F. 9. Remove the skillet from the oven and let the pork chops rest for a few minutes before serving. 10. Garnish with fresh herbs and serve hot.

For our E-Commerce initiative specifically, we’re taking the following steps to lessen our carbon footprint and protect our ecosystem: How We Help to Protect Our Nation's Forests For every order shipped, we will donate to the Arbor Day Foundation, whose mission is to replant and revitalize damaged areas of our nation’s forests. Recipe: Sheet Pan Roasted Chicken and Vegetables Ingredients 1 package Perdue Harvestland Free Range Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts 3 cloves garlic, sliced 1 lemon, zested and juiced 16 oz. baby potatoes, halved crosswise 6 medium carrots cut into large chunks and halved lengthwise 8 oz. green beans 8 oz. brussel sprouts, cut in half 1 large onion cut into slices 4 tbsp. olive oil 4-5 sprigs fresh thyme leaves 1/2 tsp. black pepper 1 tsp. salt Instructions On a sheet tray lined with foil, combine potatoes, carrots, green beans, brussels sprouts, onion and garlic. Drizzle the vegetables with 3 tablespoons olive oil and lemon zest. Toss to coat well. Place chicken breasts on top of the vegetables in the center of the sheet tray. Drizzle chicken with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Sprinkle the lemon juice, thyme, salt and black pepper evenly over the chicken breasts and vegetables. Roast chicken breasts and vegetables in a pre-heated 400 degree Fahrenheit oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender and golden brown. Chicken is done when a meat thermometer inserted in the center reaches 165°F. Let chicken rest for 2 to 3 minutes before slicing. Transfer chicken breasts to a cutting board and slice into serving pieces. Place chicken breasts on a serving platter and surround with roasted vegetables. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs if desired.

originalName: Truvia Original Calorie-Free Sweetener Packets, 400 ct.
name: Truvia Original Calorie-Free Sweetener Packets, 400 ct.
description: 400 count box of plant-based sweetner packets Sugar free and keto friendly No artificial sweeteners Suitable for people with diabetes
introduction: Sweetness is meant to be enjoyed. That's why Truvia created products meant to reduce sugar, not taste. The clean, sweet flavor contained in Truvia Natural Sweetener packets comes from nature in the form of the stevia leaf. Leaves don't dissolve well in beverages or baked goods, so we extract the sweetness from the stevia leaf. Because stevia leaf extract is 200x sweeter than sugar, we balance the sweetness with erythritol, a sweetener produced by fermentation. Erythritol is also found in fruits like grapes and pears. This gives you the white crystals you're used to without the calories. This 400-count box can be stashed at home, at work or a few packets can be thrown in your bag for on-the-go sweetness. Is Truvia the Same Thing as Stevia? The stevia plant provides the extract which is the main ingredient in Truvia sweetener. The components that make Truvia sweet are extracted from the leaves and purified. Then, a special combination of natural flavors is added to give Truvia its delicious taste. Stevia leaf packs a lot of sweetness which means a little bit goes a long way! What is Erythritol? Erythritol is what gives the sugar substitute its crystalline, sugary appearance. A fermentation process, similar to brewing beer, is used to make the erythritol. A natural yeast called Moniliella pollinis "digests" dextrose, a simple sugar. Once digested, erythritol is produced. It is then filtered and dried, forming crystals. Erythritol can be found naturally in various fruits like pears and grapes. You can also find erythritol in some wines and in soy sauce. Is Truvia Gluten-Free? Yes! Truvia sugar substitute does not contain any gluten and can be used by those on a gluten-free diet. In fact, it can be a great option for many people who have restricted diets. It can be used as a sweetener for people with Type 2 Diabetes. Truvia sugar is also acceptable for vegetarians and vegans. Plus, it is allowed on low-carb diets like Keto or Paleo, and adding it to your morning cup of coffee will not use any of your Weight Watchers points. In the kitchen, Truvia has so many applications! You can bake and cook with it just like you would the processed white sugar that is normally in your cabinet. Every sweet opportunity—from your coffee, tea, fruit, cereal and yogurt to your favorite family recipes—can be made even sweeter by using Truvía Natural Sweetener.

Slice or cube them for sandwiches, salads and burgers, or to top your toast; mash them for guacamole and baby food; or blend them into your favorite smoothie for a creamy texture. Good Fats and Fiber in Every Serving Avocados contain good fats and nearly 20 vitamins and minerals. Big-Batch Guacamole Made Simple If you’ve never made your own guacamole at home, it may seem intimidating. Have no fear—this one is quick, simple and anyone can pull it off. For a generous bowl of guacamole, mash 6 avocados with the juice of 2 limes, 1 diced white onion, and 2 tsp. salt. Stir in 6 Tbsp. chopped cilantro, 4 diced plum tomatoes, and 2 tsp. finely minced garlic. Add a few pinches of cayenne pepper, depending on how much your guests enjoy spice, then refrigerate for 1 hour before serving. Ripeness, Storage, and Fresh-Cut Tips Use these practical tips to pick the right avocado for tonight and keep the rest fresh: • Ripeness is best checked by feel, not color; a ready-to-eat avocado should have uniform softness. • To speed ripening, place avocados in a paper bag with a banana or apple, close the bag, and leave it on the counter for 24–48 hours. • Store firm or under-ripe avocados at room temperature until they reach your preferred ripeness; once ripe, refrigerate them for several days. • For clean slices and cubes (great for sandwiches and toast), choose firm-ripe avocados that yield slightly to gentle pressure; for mashing and guacamole, choose avocados that yield easily to gentle pressure. • To help cut avocado stay fresh, apply a thin layer of lemon or lime juice to the cut surface and wrap tightly with plastic wrap. For extra help keeping produce fresh longer, store fruits and vegetables with a Bluapple Carbon Saver Combo Pack . Apply a thin layer of lemon or lime juice to the cut surface and wrap tightly with plastic wrap. What can I make with these avocados besides guacamole? introduction: Create numerous dishes using this bag of baking potatoes. Russet potatoes have hearty skin that's tender when cooked. These fresh potatoes are the ideal size and texture for baking on high heat. How Can You Cook Baking Potatoes? Baking potatoes can be cooked multiple ways in the oven: Form bite-sized pieces by cutting the potatoes into chunks, tossing in olive oil and sprinkling with herbs. Make the traditional oven-baked potato and top it with chives, butter, sour cream, cheese and bacon bits. Create Hasselback Potatoes by making vertical slices all throughout the cooked fresh vegetable, inserting slices of cheese in-between and drizzling the top with olive oil. Create tempting potato skins by cutting a few potatoes lengthwise, scoop out some of the interior, brush with oil and bake until crisp. Add bacon and cheese to the inside, and place back into the oven for a few minutes. Next, top the skins with green onions and sour cream for a flavorful snack. What's in a Potato? Potatoes have been a classic dinner staple for many years and there's a good reason for that. While this fresh vegetable looks big in size, water accounts for 70-80 percent of the weight. It's also full of minerals and vitamins. A common misconception is that potatoes are unhealthy, but these vegetables can actually help to improve digestion, boost heart health, reduce cholesterol levels, strengthen the immune system and manage diabetes. Other Ways to Eat Potatoes In addition to baking, these fresh potatoes can be prepared in different ways for many recipes. Pan fry or sauté your potatoes to include with your favorite family meal. You can cut these fresh vegetables up to make tasty french fries or slice them very thin to create your very own potato chips. They're also terrific for dishes like hash browns, casseroles, mashed potato, salads and latkes. How Should I Store My Potatoes? Store your potatoes in a cool, well-ventilated place. Avoid areas that reach high temperatures or receive too much sunlight such as beneath the sink, countertops, or beside large appliances. If refrigerated, let the potato warm gradually to room temperature before cooking to avoid discoloration. When stored in temperatures lower than 50°F, potato's starch converts to sugar which can result in discoloration. Perforated plastic bags and paper bags tend to offer the best environment for extending a potatoes shelf life. No need to wash potatoes before storing because dampness can promote early spoilage.

The primary difference between bread flour and all-purpose flour is the protein content. Bread flour, like King Arthur’s, has more protein (12.7%) than all-purpose (11.7%). For context, pastry and cake flours have less, about 8% to 10%, respectively. These may seem like small differences, but they have a significant effect on how the flour behaves. The protein in flour is what forms gluten in your dough, so higher protein means more gluten. More gluten translates to stronger, stretchier dough, which is critical for a tall, airy loaf of bread.

These tender and airy bite-sized flatbreads are perfect for snacking, entertaining, or just satisfying that craving for something deliciously different. Authentically Flame-Baked for a Rich Flavor You'll love how we make our naan bites—they're flame-baked in a tandoori-style oven at a scorching 650° F, using traditional ingredients. This process gives them that rich flavor and hint of smokiness you can't get enough of. Trust us, once you try these naan bites, plain old chips just won't cut it anymore. Perfect Pairings for Your Naan Bites So, how do you enjoy these delightful morsels? Warm them up and pair them with your favorite dips, spreads, soups or curry. They're absolutely fantastic with hummus, chicken salad, cured meats, soft cheese and so much more. Go ahead and get creative with your pairings! Entertaining Made Easy Next time you're hosting a gathering, don't forget to include Member's Mark Tandoori Style Naan Bites on your menu. Your guests will love these unique and scrumptious snacks, and you'll love how easy they are to serve. Just warm, pair, and watch them disappear! Warming Instructions Conventional Oven: Heat to 400° F for 2 to 3 minutes on the middle rack of the oven. Microwave: Heat for 15-20 seconds on high heat. Air Fryer: Heat to 360° F for 1.5 to 2 minutes. Grill: Heat for 1 minute on each side until golden brown. Recipe: Roasted Red Pepper & Kale with Hummus Naan Bites Ingredients: Member's Mark Tandoori Style Naan Bites, 22.2 oz. 1 cup roasted red pepper hummus or classic hummus ⅓ cup red onion diced 1 red bell pepper sliced 1 cup kale 1 tbsp olive oil ½ cup crumbled feta cheese optional: black pepper / red pepper flakes, fresh parsley for garnish Directions: Pre heat oven to 400˚F. Spread about ½ the amount of Naan Bites from container onto a baking sheet and bake for 2-3 minutes on the middle rack of the oven. Remove from oven and set aside to slightly cool. While the Naan Bites are being cooled, place sliced pepper into a skillet and roast for 5-7 minutes, or until a bit black on either side. Once peppers are almost done, add 1 tbsp of olive oil and kale to skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes or until kale is cooked; set peppers and kale aside. Spread hummus over slightly cooled Naan Bites; add onion, red pepper, kale, and feta cheese. Add black pepper / red pepper flakes and garnish with fresh parsley if desired. Plate and enjoy! introduction: Delicious and Nutritious Cara Cara oranges are less acidic and much sweeter than most other varieties of oranges. Their flavor is described as a cross between a very sweet orange and berries, usually raspberry or blackberry. The pith is thinner, so they are less bitter and taste juicier. They have an orange exterior peel that encases a unique pink interior. This beautiful color is due to the high amounts of lycopene found in them. These oranges are available from December through May and provide good nutritional value. One Cara Cara orange provides 100% of daily vitamin C requirement, which is the most of any citrus variety. What to Look For A ripe Cara Cara feels heavy for its size, has a firm yet slightly springy texture, and emits a fragrant citrus aroma. The skin should display a bright orange hue without any traces of green. When fully mature, a Cara Cara orange typically reaches the size of a baseball. Storage Tips and Tricks Cara Cara oranges can be kept on the counter out of direct sunlight for one to two weeks. For longer storage, around a month or so, opt for the crisper drawer in the fridge. If you keep them refrigerated, make sure to bring them to room temperature before eating or using them to cook. Versatile Uses and Pairings Cara Cara oranges are great for juicing, snacking, baking, for use in recipes, or simply to eat as is. The zest and juice are great to use in a vinaigrette with whole grain mustard, white wine vinegar and olive oil – perfect for dressing a salad or greens. Cara Cara’s big juicy flavor also makes them perfect for baking and dessert. They are ideal for an orange cake, especially the glaze. Because of their natural sweetness, they are perfect for sorbet, custards and cheesecake. Cara Cara oranges are ideal on the side of roasted and charred meats such as a tri-tip roast salad with Cara Cara orange honey vinaigrette. They have a more saturated flavor than most other oranges, so use them for a prominent orange flavor. Try a Cara Cara orange cottage cheese toast or infused focaccia bread.

Cooking Instructions Prep: Pat ribs dry and season generously with your preferred rub or spices. Choose Cooking Method: Baking/Roasting: Preheat oven to 325-350°F (160-175°C). Place ribs in a baking dish or on a rack. Bake 1.5-2.5 hours, or until very tender. Grilling: Set up for indirect heat (one side hot, one side cool). Sear ribs over direct heat, then move to indirect heat. Grill 1.5-2 hours, or until very tender, turning occasionally. Slow Cooker/Braising: Place ribs in slow cooker or Dutch oven with about 1 cup of liquid (broth, sauce, etc.). Cook on low for 6-8 hours or high for 3-4 hours, until fall-apart tender. Check Doneness: Pork ribs are safe at 145°F (63°C). For ideal tender, pull-apart texture, cook bone-in country style ribs until they reach 185-205°F (85-96°C). Rest: Let ribs rest for 10-15 minutes before serving for maximum juiciness. Meal Idea - Easy Baked BBQ Country Style Ribs & Roasted Potatoes (Serves 3-4) Prep Time: ~15 minutes / Cook Time: ~2-2.5 hours Ingredients 2-3 lbs. Member's Mark Bone-In Country Style Pork Ribs 1 tbsp garlic powder 1 tsp onion powder 1 tsp salt 1/2 tsp black pepper 1 cup BBQ sauce 1.5 lbs. small potatoes (quartered) 1 tbsp olive oil Directions 1. Prep Ribs: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C). Pat ribs dry, then season generously with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. 2. Bake Ribs (Covered): Place ribs in a baking dish, cover tightly with foil, and bake for 1.5 hours. 3. Prep & Roast Potatoes: While ribs bake, toss quartered potatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper. After 1.5 hours, add potatoes to the baking dish (or a separate pan). 4. Finish Baking & Sauce: Uncover ribs, baste with BBQ sauce. Continue baking with potatoes for another 30-45 minutes (total 2-2.5 hours for ribs), flipping potatoes halfway, until ribs are tender (185-205°F internal temp) and potatoes are golden. 5. Rest & Serve: Let ribs rest 10 mins. Serve with roasted potatoes. originalName: Cholula Original Hot Sauce, 12 oz., 2 pk.
name: Cholula Original Hot Sauce, 12 oz., 2 pk.
description: Two 12 ounce bottles of Cholula Original Hot Sauce A blend of arbol and piquin peppers and signature spices, complex hot sauce with just the right amount of fiery heat Add flavor excitement to all your foods For eggs, rice and beans, beverages and even pizza For Mexican-style dishes like tacos, nachos, huevos rancheros, fajitas and salsa
introduction: Authentic Flavor with Cholula Original Hot Sauce Cholula Original Hot Sauce is a timeless classic crafted from a generations-old family recipe. Featuring a blend of arbol and piquin peppers along with regional spices, this medium-heat sauce delivers an authentic Mexican flavor that enhances any dish. From its distinctive wooden cap to the bold taste inside, every bottle is a celebration of Mexican culinary heritage. Versatile 2-Pack of 12-Ounce Bottles This 2-pack of 12-ounce bottles offers endless possibilities for adding flavor to your meals. Shake it on eggs, rice, beans, pizza, or even beverages for a flavorful kick. Whether you're enjoying traditional Mexican dishes like enchiladas and tamales or modern favorites like burrito bowls and fish tacos, Cholula Original Hot Sauce is the perfect companion. Recipe Idea: Chorizo Breakfast Burrito Elevate your breakfast with this Chorizo Breakfast Burrito recipe featuring Cholula Original Hot Sauce. With ingredients like hash browns, chorizo, scrambled eggs, avocado, and shredded Mexican cheese, this dish is packed with flavor. Simply drizzle Cholula over the filling, roll it up in a warm tortilla, and enjoy a delicious start to your day. Serve with extra hot sauce for added zest! Celebrate Great Food and Flavor Cholula Original Hot Sauce is more than just a condiment—it's a tribute to great food and Mexican roots. Whether you're spicing up your favorite recipes or exploring new culinary creations, this hot sauce brings a touch of authenticity and bold flavor to every meal. Chorizo Breakfast Burrito Servings: 4 Ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil 4 frozen hash brown patties 1/2 pound fresh Mexican chorizo sausage 1/2 cup Cholula® Original Hot Sauce 4 (10-inch) flour tortillas 4 scrambled eggs Sliced avocado 4 tbsp shredded Mexican cheese 4 tsp red onion Instructions: Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet on medium heat until shimmering. Add 4 frozen hash brown patties. Cook about 4 - 5 minutes per side or until lightly browned and crispy. Remove from skillet; set aside. Add 1/2 pound fresh Mexican chorizo sausage to skillet. Cook and crumble just until browned, about 3 - 5 minutes. Increase heat to medium-high. Return hash browns to skillet, crumbling into bite-size chunks. Drizzle with 1/2 cup Cholula® Original Hot Sauce. Cook, stirring gently until mixture is well blended, about 1 minute. To assemble burritos, divide chorizo mixture into 4 portions. Spread chorizo mixture horizontally across the bottom third of 4 warm (10-inch) flour tortillas, leaving room on bottom and sides to fold. For each burrito, top chorizo with 1 scrambled egg, sliced avocado, 1 tablespoon shredded Mexican cheese, and 1 tsp. red onion. To roll burrito, turn tortilla so that filling side is closest to you. Grasp tortilla at 8 o’clock and 4 o’clock position and fold in to cover ends of filling, forming a ‘v’ at the bottom of the tortilla. Then, fold up bottom of tortilla over topping and tuck underneath to secure. Fold in sides of tortilla (9 o’clock and 3 o’clock positions) to form a pleat, then continue to roll from the bottom up, tucking in sides as you go. Place burrito seam down in skillet on medium heat. Cook about 30 seconds to seal. Serve with additional hot sauce.

introduction: Red Potatoes have a thin skin with a vibrant, red color. They are a good choice for cooking because they bring a unique texture to any lunch or dinner meal. Red potatoes are a starchy, root vegetable that originated in Central America. Potatoes are an inexpensive stable pantry item that can have many different textures depending on the cooking process. What Is the Nutritional Value of Red Potatoes? Red potatoes are a low-fat, no-cholesterol food. A 100-gram serving of potatoes only contains 70 calories, and they are a good source of essential vitamins. Red potatoes are also a great source of dietary fiber, and they are also a reliable carbohydrate. They're rich in vitamin B, vitamin A and vitamin C. If you consume the skin, you will also get added antioxidants. Red potatoes also contain essential minerals that are needed in a well-rounded diet including thiamin, niacin, folates and pantothenic acid. How Should I Store Red Potatoes? The best way to store your 8 lb. bag of red potatoes is in a cool, dark place that is free from moisture. Before storing, you should clean your potatoes. Brush off the excess soil, and then rinse them under cool running water. Allow the potatoes to dry before storing to prevent early spoilage. Red potatoes should be kept well-ventilated, so it is best to store them in an open container. If refrigerated, allow potato to gradually warm to room temperature before cooking to reduce discoloration. If properly stored, they can last up to several months. How Can I Cook Red Potatoes? Cooking with potatoes gives you endless possibilities. There are so many red potato recipes, your only difficulty will be narrowing down the options. You can find roasted red potato recipes, baked red potato recipes, oven-roasted red potato recipes, mashed red potato recipes and so much more. Some red potato recipes call for peeling the potatoes and some call for leaving the skins on. They can be cut into cubes, scalloped, diced, sliced or fried. Red potatoes are good with or without seasoning.

Cooking Instructions Connecticut Style Ingredients: 2 lbs Cooked Lobster Meat 8 Split-Top Buns 1 Seasoning Packet 16 tbsp Butter, Divided (not included) 1 Lemon (not included) Directions: Preparation: Unbox the ingredients. Handle the dry ice with care, avoiding skin contact. Store the lobster meat in the refrigerator to thaw. Once thawed, drain the lobster meat thoroughly. Prepare the Buns: Brush the buns with 8 tbsp of melted butter and toast them in a pan over medium heat for about 45 seconds per side, until golden. Keep the toasted buns warm in the oven. Cook Lobster: Heat the remaining 8 tbsp of butter in a pan over medium heat. Add the lobster meat and squeeze lemon over it. Cook for about 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. Assemble: Remove the warm buns from the oven. Fill each bun with the buttery lobster mixture. Season with the packet contents to taste. Serve: Enjoy your Connecticut Style Lobster Rolls warm and buttery! Maine Style Ingredients: 2 lbs Cooked Lobster Meat 8 Split-Top Buns 1 Seasoning Packet 1/2 cup Mayonnaise (not included) 8 tbsp Melted Butter (not included) 1/2 Lemon (not included) Directions: Preparation: Unbox the ingredients. Safely handle dry ice; avoid direct contact with skin. Refrigerate the lobster meat until it is thawed. Once thawed, drain the lobster meat in a strainer to remove excess liquid. Prepare the Buns: Brush the buns with melted butter and toast them in a pan over medium heat for about 45 seconds per side, or until lightly golden. Keep the toasted buns warm in the oven. Mix Filling: In a mixing bowl, combine the lobster meat with mayonnaise and juice from the half lemon. Stir well until the mixture is evenly coated. Assemble: Remove the warm buns from the oven. Fill each bun generously with the lobster mixture. Sprinkle with seasoning from the packet to taste. Serve: Enjoy your Maine style lobster rolls while they are fresh!

introduction: Whole white mushrooms are a staple of the well-equipped kitchen and they add a meaty texture to your meals. With a flavor that is mild and earthy, these fresh mushrooms can easily be added to a salad, put on top of a pizza, or added to a breakfast omelet. You'll love the added flavor and texture that these whole white mushrooms bring to your meatless meals! How Do I Store Whole White Mushrooms? Fresh mushrooms have a fairly short shelf life, so it's best to use them as early as you possibly can. If you're storing them for use at a later date, leave the package sealed until you are ready to cook and eat them. If you only use a partial package of mushrooms, keep the remainder in a paper bag and store in the refrigerator. The paper helps absorb moisture, which will keep them fresher for a longer period of time. Mushroom Nutrition White button mushrooms contain natural proteins, and are also endowed with vitamins, minerals and antioxidants. They can be a good source of vitamin B12, which is great for those on vegan or vegetarian diets since there are few plants that provide this essential vitamin. Fresh mushrooms are also a low-fat, low-calorie food that does not contain any cholesterol. Cooking mushrooms within your various meals will give you many of the essential minerals you need like manganese, zinc, copper and iodine. How Do I Cook Whole White Mushrooms? There are many white mushroom recipes that are healthy and delicious. However, before you cook them, you should make sure that they have been properly cleaned. Brush off the dirt from the white button mushrooms and wash them briefly under cool running water. You want to avoid soaking or peeling mushrooms. In recipes that simmer for an extended period, it is best to add the mushrooms towards the end of the simmer time for the best flavor. Recipe: Classic Stuffed Mushrooms What You'll Need 24 ounces white button mushrooms 3/4 pound pork or turkey sausage 6 ounces cream cheese Softened 1/3 cup panko bread crumbs 4 tablespoons freshly grated Parmesan cheese 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt Small or chopped basil leaves for garnish How to Make It Prep Time: 30 Minutes | Cook Time: 35 Minutes | Yield: 21 Mushrooms Remove the stem from each mushroom. Spray a baking dish large enough to hold all the mushrooms, about 9" x 13", with non-stick cooking spray. Place the mushroom caps upside down in a baking dish. Cook the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat until no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Break it up into small pieces as it cooks. Reduce the heat to medium and stir in the cream cheese until melted, about 2 minutes. Add the panko bread crumbs and remove the skillet from the heat. Stir until all ingredients are combined. Add 2 tablespoons of Parmesan and the salt. Stir well. Let sit until cool enough to handle. Preheat the oven to 375°F. Fill each mushroom cap with an equal amount of the sausage stuffing, mounding it high over the mushroom. Bake for 25 minutes, until the filling is bubbly and the mushrooms are tender. Sprinkle the remaining 2 tablespoons of Parmesan over the mushrooms just as you pull them out of the oven. Garnish with basil before serving.

Smoked Gouda Cheese and Macaroni Bake Recipe Prep time: 15 mins | Cook time: 15 mins | Servings: 4 Ingredients: 1 (approximately 1.74 lbs.) block Member’s Mark Hardwood Smoked Gouda Cheese 2 c Member’s Mark Elbow Noodles 6 tbsp Member’s Mark Unsalted Butter, divided 1 tsp Member’s Mark Sea Salt, divided ¼ tsp Member’s Mark Garlic Powder 3-4 slices bread 2 tbsp Member’s Mark All Purpose Flour 1 c Member’s Mark Milk ¼ c Member’s Mark Heavy Whipping Cream Instructions: Preheat oven to 425ºF and line an 8x8” baking dish with aluminum foil. Begin cooking the noodles according to package instructions, drain and set aside. While cooking noodles, use a cheese grater, shred half the block of cheese into a bowl, (about 4 ¼ cups of shredded cheese) set aside. Melt 4 tablespoons of butter in a microwave-safe bowl. Then stir in 1/2 teaspoon salt and garlic powder. Tear the bread slices into small crumbled pieces and toss in the melted butter mixture, set aside. In the same pot the noodles were cooked in, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, over medium heat. Slowly, stir in flour and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt until well combined. Whisk in milk and cream. Raise the heat to high, continuously whisking to a boil until thickening begins; about 3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in shredded cheese until melted. Add the noodles to the sauce coating well and pour into the lined baking dish. Top the mac and cheese with the buttery bread crumbs and desired amount of remaining cheese. Place in the oven and bake for 10 minutes. Raise the oven temperature to broil and toast the top for 1-2 minutes, or until golden brown. Serve immediately. introduction: What Are the Health Benefits of Fresh Pineapple? Golden pineapple has lots of health benefits! Chock full of vitamin C, manganese and more, the sweet pineapple is a perfect addition to your day. What's great is that it tastes like candy and is also good for you! There are so many delicious ways to use this item so that you get the health benefits of eating pineapple. How Can I Tell When Golden Pineapple is Ripe? Depending on the type of pineapple, it may be perfectly ripe when the scales are green. In the event that you want to be extra sure that you have a sweet pineapple in your hands, opt for one with yellow scales. If it gets darker than yellow and starts to turn orange, your pineapple fruit is overripe. Give your golden pineapple a little squeeze. If it feels a tiny bit soft, the flesh has been ripened. You can also smell the bottom of the pineapple fruit. If it is fragrant and sweet, it is ready to be eaten. Some people even prefer to store their pineapples upside down to redistribute the juice and sugar so that each bite is perfectly sweet. Golden Pineapple Recipes There are so many different uses for a sweet pineapple. Chop it up and use it to marinate everything from steak to pork. Not only will the pineapple fruit add flavor but the acid will tenderize the meat. You can also blend it up in smoothies and add it to your juices for natural sweetness and a tropical twist. We also love the idea of baking with pineapples. Use it to make a pineapple upside down cake or pineapple pie. Prefer eating pineapples raw? While they taste fantastic as is, for some fun twists you can sprinkle some salt on it for a unique flavor or even top it with whipped cream for a scrumptious combination.

introduction: Our Member's Mark™️ Pork Carnitas turn any meal into a fiesta! We take carnitas, which means "little meats" in Spanish, to the next level by using seasonings inspired by the Mexican state of Michoacán, the birthplace of carnitas. Marbled cuts of pork shoulder are braised low and slow, resulting in small morsels of tender, juicy meat that can be used in all of your favorite dishes. Get Restaurant-Style Pork Carnitas Right at Home Carnitas are a delicious and versatile protein option for sandwiches, salads, wraps, tacos and burritos. This is a perfect dish for game day appetizers or after-school snacking. Prepare the carnitas in your microwave or air fryer for meat that's crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Cooking Instructions OVEN: Preheat oven to 350°F. Remove product from pouch and place into an oven-safe pan. Cover with a tight-fitting lid or aluminum foil and heat for about 15 minutes or until product reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. MICROWAVE: Place pouch in a microwave safe dish and cut 2-3 small slits in the package. Microwave on high heat for about 6 minutes or until product reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. STOVE TOP: Remove the product from the pouch, place into a large sauté pan and cover with a tight-fitting lid. Heat over medium-low for about 10 minutes or until product reaches an internal temperature of 165°F, gently stirring every few minutes to ensure even heating. AIR FRYER: Preheat air fryer to 350°F. Remove pork carnitas from packaging and place into preheated air fryer basket. Allow the pork carnitas to cook for 10 minutes (you may shake the air fryer basket halfway through to ensure even cooking). Remove the meat from the air fryer and transfer to a heat-stable container. Using a fork, gently shred the pork carnitas to your desired consistency. Serve. Powdered infant formulas are NOT sterile and should NOT be fed to premature infants or infants who might have immune problems unless directed and supervised by your baby’s doctor. introduction: A 5 lb. bag of Gala apples is an easy way to stock up on crisp, juicy fruit for everyday snacking and kitchen prep. With a balanced tart-and-sweet flavor and a bright bicolor appearance, Gala apples are a versatile choice for lunchboxes, salads, and baking. Each bag includes approximately 9–12 apples. Flavor Profile and Pairing Suggestions The Gala apple is a delightful blend of tart and sweet, making it versatile for pairing with a variety of flavors. It harmonizes exceptionally well with bold, distinctive flavors such as curry powder, fresh ginger, tarragon, basil, and chives. The savory flavors complement the Gala apple's moderate sweetness, while overly sweet ingredients may overshadow its unique taste. Selection and Storage When choosing Gala apples, look for a bright, vibrant bicolor appearance. The apple should feel firm and solid to the touch. To enjoy, rinse thoroughly under cold running water for about 10–20 seconds. For storage, keep the apples in a cool, dry place, preferably in the refrigerator's crisper drawer or a plastic bag with small holes. Ways to Enjoy With 9–12 apples per bag, there are plenty for grab-and-go snacks and multiple recipes. Slice and serve as a quick, healthy bite, or chop over oatmeal or yogurt for breakfast. Add fresh slices to a salad for a sweet-tart crunch, or include on a party platter or cheese board for entertaining. Gala apples also work well in classic baked dishes like pies, crumbles, or applesauce. Health Benefits Gala apples are not just tasty, but they also offer health benefits. They are high in fiber, vitamin C, and natural antioxidants, and may support blood sugar control. However, individual health benefits can vary and it's always best to consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice. History of the Gala Apple The Gala apple was born in 1930s New Zealand — a cross between a Kidd's Orange Red and a Golden Delicious. The name reportedly came after Queen Elizabeth II enjoyed the apple during a visit to New Zealand. Frequently Asked Questions What do Gala apples taste like? How can I serve Gala apples for entertaining? Include slices on a party platter or cheese board-style spread for an easy, crowd-pleasing addition. Where did the Gala apple originate? Developed in New Zealand in the 1930s by crossing Kidd's Orange Red and Golden Delicious apples. Reportedly named after Queen Elizabeth II enjoyed one during a visit. Can I use Gala apples in savory recipes? Yes. Their moderate sweetness pairs well with savory ingredients like curry powder, ginger, and fresh herbs, making them excellent in appetizer and main course dishes.

What to Look For When lemons are ripe, they have a yellow hue and their size ranges from two to three inches. If the lemon is firm, it's likely at its peak of ripeness; a squishy texture, on the other hand, may mean that the fruit is past its prime. Storage Tips for Lemons Lemons can be stored at room temperature for up to a week. Lemons can last up to a month in the refrigerator. Store them in a crisper drawer or on a shelf. They can be placed in an airtight container or resealable bag to prevent them from drying out. Lemons can also be frozen up to four months either whole or cut into slices. The lemon juice can also be frozen in ice cube trays. Versatile Uses and Pairings Lemons are ideal for juicing, used in dressings and marinades and as a beverage flavor. Lemons pair well with many foods, including other citrus, seafood, herbs and spices. For a seafood-inspired dish, try lemon-garlic pasta with salmon or shrimp. Use lemons with chicken to create a chicken picatta or skillet lemon chicken with spinach. Lemons can add flavor to water or tea; and used in salad dressing and a vegetable marinade. introduction: Make dinner even more delicious with King's Hawaiian Original Dinner Roll. These fluffy rolls are a cut above your average dinner roll, crafted with Hawaiian sweet bread using a traditional, time-honored family recipe. The Hawaiian sweet rolls are also terrific for sliders and bite-sized sandwiches, for a tropical twist and a taste of aloha. The King's Hawaiian Original Dinner Roll Story King's Hawaiian bread got its start in Hilo, Hawaii in the 1950s by Robert Taira, a young man with a big passion for baking. Using the best local ingredients, Taira created a bread that was irresistibly soft, fluffy and just the right amount of sweet for a taste like none other. King's Hawaiian sweet bread became a local staple, spreading through the Hawaiian Islands and eventually to the U.S. mainland, bringing a little of the Aloha Spirit to breadbaskets and sandwiches from coast to coast. Today, the Taira family's legacy and original recipe continues, showcased in everything from King's Hawaiian rolls and round breads to mini sub rolls, hot dog and hamburger buns. The delightful breads add just the right balance to everything from deli sandwiches to French toast--and they even taste fantastic straight from the bag! What's the Best Way to Prepare King's Hawaiian Sweet Rolls? Like all King's Hawaiian sweet bread varieties, these Hawaiian rolls taste soft, sweet and delicious right from the bag. For the softest, fluffiest, warmest rolls, heat them at 300 degrees Fahrenheit in a conventional oven for two to three minutes. If you like your King's Hawaiian sweet rolls a little crispier, heat them for four to five minutes. This value pack includes two 16-piece trays of rolls, ready to heat and eat.

introduction: Kiwi is an intriguing fruit with fuzzy brown skin, glistening green flesh, and a sweet and tart taste that leaves you hydrated and nourished. Green Kiwi offers an antioxidant powerhouse that makes it a smart choice for snacks and meals. What Vitamins Do Kiwis Contain? Kiwi is no ordinary fruit. It has been valued around the globe for centuries for its nutritional properties. If you thought oranges had the most vitamin C, think again! Green kiwi has nearly double the amount as both oranges and lemons. Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that helps eliminate free radicals that cause cellular damage. You also get the added boost of immune support to keep you healthy during flu season. One kiwi and you also get a blend of vitamins A, B6, B12, E, potassium, calcium, iron and magnesium. Keep your skin, bones and vision young and beautiful by enjoying this fruit often. Kiwi also contains folate, a vitamin that helps pregnant women and young children to maintain proper growth. Do Kiwis Have Other Health Benefits? Studies show that kiwi fruit also releases small doses of serotonin, which may help aid in sleep and relaxation after eating. This exotic fruit is also a good source of fiber. Foods high in fiber help to keep you full for longer and aid in regulating blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol levels. Kiwi Fruit Has Many Uses There are multiple kiwi fruit uses to try and share with friends. Spruce up your yogurt or cereal in the morning with slices of kiwi. Decorate a dessert for friends with the beautiful green interior. Try sliced kiwi on a summer salad. Kiwi fruit also tastes delicious in a variety of smoothies.

Bananas, pineapples, melons, mangos, plums, peaches and pears: These meant to be stored at room temperature in a cool spot with ample circulation until ripe. Once they’re ripe, transfer them to the fridge until you’re ready to eat them; this will slow down the ripening process. Avocados and tomatoes: Yes, these are fruits! Store them at room temperature away from direct sunlight and use when ripe. Grapes, lemons, oranges and limes: Store them in the fridge’s produce/crisper drawer until ready to use. For cut-up citrus fruits, wrap them tightly in plastic wrap and store in an airtight container or zip-top bag in the fridge. Apples: This is a toss-up. Apples can be stored in a cool, dry dark place (for long-term storage) or in the fridge (if you know you’ll eat them within a few weeks). Apples emit ethylene gas which will speed up the ripening process for other produce so it’s best to store them separately. Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries and raspberries: Transfer the berries from the clamshell packaging into a bag or container lined with a paper or cloth towel. Wash right before you’re ready to eat them. Pre-washing berries will cause them to get soggy. Freeze any unused fruit by cutting them into bite-sized pieces, laying them on a flat sheet with parchment paper and placing them in the freezer. Once frozen, remove the fruit from sheet and store in a plastic bag or container.

Fluffy and fat-free, Parade cotton candy makes a delightful snack for adults and children. The History Of Cotton Candy This nostalgic confection can be traced back to the 15th century. Introduced as "Fairy Floss" at the 1904 World's Fair, the machine-spun sugar was invented by William Morrison and John C. Wharton. A similar apparatus was constructed and patented by Joseph Lascaux in 1921, during which time cotton candy got its name. How's Cotton Candy Made? Cotton candy is made by heating up sugar and spinning it into fine threads. Flavor and color is added by many manufacturers. introduction: Delicious and Nutritious Fresh jalapeños are known for their bold, zesty flavor and moderate heat that can add a fiery kick to any dish. Jalapeños are packed with natural goodness. The green skin is smooth and firm, while the seeds and inner membranes contain the majority of the heat. When selecting fresh jalapeños, always look for peppers that are firm, glossy, and smooth. Jalapeños are not only delicious but also offer a variety of health benefits. High in vitamin C, they help boost your immune system, promote healthy skin, and assist in collagen production. Bring the Heat and Flavor to Your Dish Jalapeños pair wonderfully with a wide range of foods, bringing both heat and flavor to any dish. For a quick and easy recipe, try a Spicy Guacamole dip: Ingredients Avocados: 3 ripe, slightly soft to the touch Jalapeño: 1 whole, finely diced (remove seeds for less heat, leave them in for a spicy kick) Lime Juice: 2–3 tablespoons (about 1 freshly squeezed lime) Onion: ½ cup finely chopped white or red onion Garlic: 1-2 cloves, finely minced or pressed Cilantro: ¼ cup chopped fresh leaves and tender stems Tomato: 1 medium Roma tomato, seeded and diced Seasoning: ½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste Instructions Prep the base: Halve the avocados, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a large mixing bowl. Mash: Add the lime juice, minced garlic, and salt. Use a fork or potato masher to mash the avocado until it reaches your desired texture—leave it a bit chunky for the best mouthfeel. Mix in aromatics: Gently stir in the diced jalapeño, chopped onion, and fresh cilantro. Fold in tomatoes: Carefully fold in the diced tomatoes last so they keep their shape. Taste and serve: Taste the guacamole and adjust the salt and lime juice as needed. Serve immediately with your favorite tortilla chips, or use as a topping for tacos. SiCar Farms A family own company with 30 years of experience in produce that originated in Mexico fields. We grow, We pack, and We distribute our own products throughout the world. We value the certification mechanisms for continuous improvement, innovation, research, and development. We respect the earth; we incorporate environmentally friendly strategies and technologies and our commitment to society is a priority. Our mission is to be the best fresh produce supplier with the highest quality standards to the final consumer through the effort and development of our people and business partners. At SiCar Farms, we are committed to sustainability and ethical practices. We work closely with local farmers to ensure that our fresh jalapeños are grown using eco-friendly methods. Tips for Storing and Handling To store fresh jalapeños, keep them in the vegetable drawer of your fridge where they’ll stay fresh for 1-2 weeks. When handling fresh jalapeños, it's advisable to wear gloves to avoid skin irritation from the capsaicin, the compound that gives peppers their heat. If you don’t use gloves, be sure to wash your hands thoroughly afterward and avoid touching your face, particularly your eyes.

introduction: Asparagus: A Nutritional Powerhouse Asparagus is not just a delicious vegetable, it's also a superfood packed with vitamins and antioxidants. Low in calories, sodium, and fat, asparagus can contribute to a healthy diet and may help reduce the risk of heart disease and diabetes. Available year-round, asparagus is a versatile ingredient that can be used in a variety of dishes, from soups and pastas to salads. Whether you enjoy it hot, cold, or grilled, asparagus comes in a variety of colors and sizes to add a touch of elegance to any meal. Best Way to Store Asparagus Fresh asparagus will keep for approximately one week in the refrigerator when stored by trimming stalk ends and standing the asparagus up in a mug or jar of 1-1/2 to 2 inches of water. Loosely cover the tops with plastic wrap. Asparagus Risotto Recipe Ingredients: 1.5 cups Aborio rice 1 cup dry white wine 1 onion - finely chopped 1 lb. asparagus (~half the bag) 3/4 cup grated parmesan 2 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil 4 garlic cloves - finely chopped 5 cups chicken (or vegetable) broth Salt & Pepper to taste Instructions: Warm broth in a saucepan over low heat. In a large sauté pan, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Sauté onion and garlic. Add Aborio rice and cook, stirring constantly, for 2-3 minutes. Add wine and cook until all liquid is absorbed. Add broth, 1/2 cup at a time, stirring occasionally and waiting until it is absorbed before adding more. Meanwhile in a sauté pan, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Saute asparagus until bright green and slightly tender (about 3-4 minutes). Once broth is completely absorbed into the risotto, add asparagus, season with salt and pepper, and stir in the parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.

Cooking Instructions Cook From Thawed: remove vacuum sealed film from tray and thaw in refrigerator overnight. Do not refreeze thawed lobster. Store thawed lobster in the refrigerator and use within two days. Boil (Preferred Method): Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Gently add tails to water and boil for approximately 5-7 minutes. Meal Idea - Lobster Mac and Cheese (4-6 Servings) Ingredients 3-4 Member's Mark warm water lobster tails 1 cup breadcrumbs 4 tbsp. Member's Mark unsalted butter 2 tbsp. all-purpose flour 2 cups Member's Mark whole milk 2 cups Member's Mark shredded sharp cheddar cheese 1.5 cups shredded gruyere cheese 1/3 cup Member's Mark shredded parmesan cheese 2 tbsp. mascarpone cheese 1/2 lb. pasta (cooked according to package directions) Salt and pepper, to taste 2 tbsp. fresh chives, for garnish Directions 1. Preheat oven to 425°F and cook lobster tails according to package instructions. 2. When cool, remove lobster meat and dice. Set aside. 3. In a bowl, melt half the butter and pour over breadcrumbs. Stir and set aside. 4. In a large saucepan, melt remaining butter over medium-low heat. 5. Add flour and whisk, for about a minute. 6. Slowly add milk, while whisking. Increase heat to medium and stir occasionally until it starts to bubble. The sauce will thicken enough to coat the back of a spoon. 7. Add salt and pepper to taste. 8. Add sharp cheddar, gruyere and parmesan cheeses, one handful at a time, while whisking. When one handful is melted, add the next. 9. When all shredded cheese has been added, add the mascarpone and stir. 10. Remove from heat. 11. Toss cooked pasta with sauce and 1/2 of the lobster meat, reserving about 1/2 for the top. 12. Pour into a bake dish and top with reserved lobster meat and breadcrumbs. 13. Bake until golden brown and bubbly, for about 10 minutes. Garnish with fresh chives. 14. Serve immediately. introduction: Taste tradition and goodness in every drop of Hellmann's Real Mayonnaise. Hellmann's is a true American original, featuring simple ingredients, a rich, creamy texture and a tangy taste that's made it the nation's leading brand. Hellmann's is crafted with care to ensure that it always tastes terrific, whether it's spread on burgers or sandwiches, incorporated into your favorite dips and dressings, or blended into potato, tuna, seafood and egg salads. The Key to Fantastic Dips? Hellmann’s Mayo! Hellmann's® Real Mayonnaise can be used in a myriad of ways in various recipes. Its rich, creamy texture and signature tangy taste makes it an ideal spread for burgers and sandwiches, infusing them with a delightful flavor. Beyond that, it can also be incorporated into dips and dressings, adding a creamy balance to the tang of vinaigrettes or the spice of salsa. Try this Baked Spinach and Artichoke Dip or the Disappearing Buffalo Chicken Dip , perfect for game day or any ga thering. Furthermore, Hellmann's® Real Mayonnaise can be blended into salads like potato, tuna, seafood, or egg, enhancing their taste and lending them a luscious, creamy texture. Available in squeezable bottles, it is easy to use in any recipe, making it a versatile addition to your kitchen. For more tasty recipes, visit the Sam’s Club Recipe Hub ! What Makes Hellmann's Real Mayonnaise So Special? Since its early days, Hellmann's has always been real mayonnaise, featuring only a few ingredients. It gets its creaminess from just vegetable oil and cage-free eggs, with at least 50 percent eggs in every jar. Its signature tang comes from vinegar. It's also a remarkably healthy mayonnaise, packed in omega-3s and is gluten free. Hellmann's real mayonnaise is also certified Kosher. The Hellmann's Real Mayonnaise History Hellman's real mayonnaise got its start in 1913 when its namesake, Richard Hellmann opened up a delicatessen in New York City with his wife Margaret. By 1920, Hellman began selling his signature sauces, including his famous mayonnaise spread, already regarded as the best mayonnaise in the city. Hellman sold two versions of his recipe, including one he regarded as the best tasting mayonnaise; his favorite version featured blue ribbons on the jars. The blue ribbon imagery remains to this day, as well as the famous recipe. Installation Overview To install, insert the four threaded spindle rods into the corners of the gate and adjust the wheels so the rubber feet touch the walls. Important Safety Warnings Always install the gate exactly as directed in the manual. Improper installation can cause serious injury. Stop using the gate once your child can climb over or push it loose. Use wall cups at the top of stairs, and never use the gate near a pool. introduction: Keep your business stocked with Member's Mark™ Premium Cane Sugar (12.5 lbs., 2,000 ct.). It comes in single-serve packets that allow customers or employees to grab exactly how much they need. A Convenient Sweet Besides being sweet and a non-GMO product, Member's Mark Premium Cane Sugar is only 10 calories per pack. It's finely granulated to easily dissolve into warm liquids like tea and coffee. This pure cane sugar can also be used to sweeten fresh fruit. It comes in a convenient box containing 2,000 packets that can be stored in a pantry or cabinet. Pure Cane Sugar Cane sugar is made from sugar cane. The plant is harvested and sent to a mill where the juice is extracted by diffusion or with water. The liquid is then clarified and heated to create a syrup. The syrup is concentrated through evaporators, the water is removed and then sugar crystals are formed. The raw sugar crystals have a brown, molasses coating that can go through a carbonation process or be bleached by sulfur dioxide to produce a whiter color. Granulated sugar has the molasses refined out of it. The fine crystals don't cake together, making it ideal for baking, beverages or sprinkling onto food. Great for Food Service Operations These sugar packets are terrific for concession stands, restaurants and cafeterias. They can be placed into large condiment bins or inside of small holders on tables. The cane sugar packets are also ideal for break rooms and waiting areas. introduction: Find a great variety of exceptionally fresh and delicious produce at your local Sam's Club store, including the versatile vegetable cauliflower (1 ct.). Cauliflower is a truly unique vegetable that can be eaten on its own as a healthy snack, or prepared with some of your favorite recipes as part of a hearty side dish. But that's not all that cauliflower can do for your diet and your overall health. There are many great cauliflower recipes out there that can transform your high fat and high carb foods into meals that are much healthier for you and your family. Can Cauliflower Be Used as a Healthy Carb Alternative? The cauliflower vegetable is a healthy alternative to using so many high-carb ingredients in your favorite recipes. You can mash and blend up cauliflower to a consistency similar to mashed potatoes. Cauliflower can be used to make various types of carb-free breads and crusts. It can also be finely chopped and used as an alternative to rice. Fresh cauliflower is great to eat all on its own, or steamed along with broccoli, carrots and other fresh vegetables for a tasty side dish that is full of flavor but low on carbs. What Vitamins and Nutrients Are Found in Cauliflower? Cauliflower is high in vitamin C. It is also a good source of vitamin B6 and vitamin K. This delicate vegetable can be incorporated into a variety of meals to help you eat healthier. Cauliflower is also an excellent source of fiber and protein. Keep it inside your refrigerator to maximize its shelf life and to keep it fresher longer. Stock up and save on your family's favorite fruits and vegetables the next time you visit your local Club. Add fresh cauliflower to your shopping list and discover the many different ways it can be prepared. Recipe: Roasted Buffalo Cauliflower Bites What You'll Need 1 large head cauliflower , cut into bite-size florets 3/4 cup flour 3/4 cup water 1 teaspoon garlic powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon pepper 1 cup Buffalo sauce How to Make It Preheat oven to 450 F. Line a baking sheet with foil, spray with cooking oil and set aside. In a large bowl, combine flour, water, garlic powder, salt & pepper. Mix until batter is smooth. Add the cauliflower florets to the batter and toss to coat completely. Place florets in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, shaking off excess batter before arranging. Cook the cauliflower in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and place cauliflower in a bowl with the Buffalo sauce. Mix well making sure each floret is coated with the sauce. Place the cauliflower florets back on the same baking sheet in a single layer. Broil in the preheated oven for another 5-10 minutes or until fork tender. Serve with dip/dressing of choice. introduction: FIJI Natural Artesian Water is economically packaged smooth-tasting water that comes in BPA-free bottles that are conveniently sized to keep you hydrated when you're on the go. If you're looking for something truly exceptional in your drinking water, Fiji Natural Artesian Water is the right choice for you. Does FIJI Natural Artesian Water Really Come from Fiji? Yes! Fiji is an island in the Pacific Ocean that's over 1,500 miles from the nearest continent. The trade winds of the equatorial region mark the start of FIJI Artesian Water's long journey through one of the most pristine ecosystems remaining in the world. In the Fijian islands, rainfall slowly filters through volcanic rock, collecting in an ancient sustainable artesian aquifer deep within the earth where it is protected from external elements. It's the way nature intended water to be. Untouched by man. FIJI Water is Earth’s Finest Water because it has more than double the electrolytes as the other two top premium bottled water brands, and ours are naturally occurring whereas theirs are added. Rain slowly filters through volcanic rock, giving FIJI Water a perfectly balanced 7.7 pH, natural minerals and electrolytes, and its signature, soft smooth taste. What is Artesian Water? Artesian water is forced to the surface by natural pressure to Fiji water's natural source. FIJI Artesian Water is untouched by human contact right up until you open the cap and it touches your lips—a truly rare experience in today's processed world. Enjoy your drinking water exactly as it was meant to be, perfectly natural and unencumbered by man. Drink FIJI Artesian Water with pride knowing that FIJI donates one percent of its revenue in support of the environment. Made With 100% Recycled Plastic We are proud to announce that FIJI Water’s 330 ml and 500 ml bottles are now made of 100% recycled plastic.* *Bottle only. Order Online and Pick Up This Imported Treat at Your Favorite Sam's Club Location With a few easy clicks on Sam's Club website, you can order this unique water from one of the world's most pristine ecosystems. Simply pick up your order at your local Sam's Club and enjoy this pure and natural FIJI Artesian Water bottled at the source to ensure its untouched quality and flavor. Fiji Water Foundation Gives Back Since its founding in 2007, The FIJI Water Foundation has supported the communities where we live and work, including providing health care access to local communities, building educational facilities, and helping preserve the Sovi Basin rainforest.

description: Bulk case sale: 2 lamb loins per bag, 10 bags per case, 20 loins total Approx. 4 loin chops per pound Grill or pan fry over medium/high heat to internal temperature of 140-145°F for medium doneness Product of Australia
introduction: Tender and delicious all-natural lamb loin chops from Australia. Raised on open pastures. The perfect item to grill, pan fry or broil for you and your guests. Recipe: Mediterranean-Spiced Lamb Chops Lamb chops are the centerpiece of this easy recipe, rubbed with a simple mixture of fresh lemon zest and herbs. While the chops cook, complete the meal with a five-minute couscous, tossed with chickpeas and pistachios. This beautiful meal is ready in 25 minutes, and makes a perfect summer family dish. Ingredients 2 tablespoons olive oil 1 tablespoon dried Italian seasoning or herbs de Provence 2 tablespoons grated lemon zest 8 lamb loin chops (about 1-inch thick each ) 1 ¼ cups chicken broth or water 1 cup uncooked couscous 1 cup rinsed drained canned chickpeas 2 tablespoons chopped pistachio nuts 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley leaves Directions Heat a grill pan over high heat until smoking. While the grill is heating, stir the oil, Italian seasoning and half the lemon zest in a small bowl. Season the lamb with salt and pepper. Rub the oil mixture on the lamb and let stand for 15 minutes. Add the lamb chops onto the grill pan and sear for about 5 minutes. Turn the lamb over and cook for 5 minutes more or until the internal temperature reaches 135°F for medium. (for best results, cover and let the lamb stand for 5 minutes). While the lamb is cooking, heat the broth to a boil in a 1 ½ quart saucepan. Stir in the couscous. Cover and remove from the heat. Let stand for 5 minutes. Fluff the couscous with a fork, then stir in the chickpeas, remaining lemon zest, pistachios and parsley. Serve the lamb with the couscous. To broil the lamb chops, position the rack 6 inches from the heat and heat the broiler to medium-high. Broil the lamb on the rack in a broiler pan for about 5 minutes per side or until the internal temperature reaches 135°F. for medium. Ingredient Note: If you have chickpeas left over in the can, they're great roasted at 375°F. until crisp, then tossed while hot with a little kosher salt for a delicious snack! Just make sure to rinse and pat them dry before roasting.

introduction: No measuring or mixing required with quick and easy Pillsbury Refrigerated Crescent Roll Dough. Fresh from the oven, every bite will remind you of that home-cooked feeling you love. The Pillsbury Brand Story Starting with a few flour mills on the banks of the Mississippi River in 1869, Pillsbury has been helping families make memories through food for over 150 years. They continue that tradition by bringing easy, freshly baked meals to your table with Crescents, Biscuits, Cinnamon Rolls, Cookies and Pie Crust (with help from the Pillsbury Doughboy, of course!). Pillsbury strives to make homemade moments extra special through products and recipes, which help make cooking and baking easy, affordable and convenient for even the busiest families. Beef Wellington for Two Recipe Perfectly cooked beef and a crisp crescent crust make this the perfect way to quickly serve a favorite. Recipe and image courtesy of Pillsbury. Ingredients: 1/8 teaspoon pepper 2 beef tenderloin steaks, 1.5" thick (6 oz. each) 2 teaspoons olive oil 2 tablespoons sun-dried tomato pesto sauce and spread (from 8-oz. jar) 1 can (4 oz.) Pillsbury™ refrigerated crescent rolls 1 egg, slightly beaten 1 tablespoon cold water Steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Line small cookie sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle pepper on both sides of steaks. In heavy 10-inch skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add steaks; cook about 1 minute on each side, turning once, or until browned. Transfer steaks to plate. Spread top of each with 1 tablespoon pesto. Cover with plastic wrap; let stand 20 minutes at room temperature to cool down for easier handling. Meanwhile, on lightly floured work surface, separate dough into 2 rectangles; firmly press perforations to seal. Roll out each rectangle into 5 1/2-inch squares. With 1 1/2- to 2-inch heart-shaped cutter, cut 2 heart shapes from 2 corners of each dough square; set hearts aside. Place 1 steak pesto side down in the center of 1 dough square. Fold opposite corners up and around steak; repeat with the remaining 2 corners. Smooth and shape dough to encase steak; place seam side down on cookie sheet. Repeat with remaining steak and dough square. In a small bowl, beat egg and water well with fork or whisk. Lightly brush top and sides of dough with egg mixture. Place 2 dough hearts on top of each overlapping slightly; lightly brush hearts with egg mixture. Bake 22 to 25 minutes or until crust is golden brown and thermometer inserted in center of steak reads 145°F. Let stand at room temperature 3 minutes before serving. (Temperature will rise at least 10° to 15° during standing time.) Expert Tips: A traditional Beef Wellington is an entire fillet of beef that has been covered with liver pâté or a seasoned mushroom mixture, wrapped in pastry and baked. These individual Wellingtons are perfect for a special Valentine’s dinner. If beef tenderloin steaks are irregular in shape, tie with kitchen string before browning. Remove string before wrapping in the dough. introduction: Hot and flaky biscuits are a great addition to any morning meal. With Pillsbury Southern Style Biscuits you get ready to serve biscuits without the hassle of doing it yourself. How to Store Pillsbury Southern Style Biscuits? It would be best if you stored Pillsbury Southern Style Biscuits in a cool, dry place or the refrigerator for freshness and use them by the best by date printed on the package. If you know you are not going to use them all by the expiration date, you can put them in the freezer. You do not have to thaw them before cooking. However, they may need a few extra minutes to warm all the way through. How Do You Heat Southern Style Biscuits? You can take these out and warm them all at once in an oven at 400°F for between five and 10 minutes. The exact time may vary from oven to oven, so you should check them at five minutes. They are ready when they are warmed to your liking. Some consumers found that lining the tray with a moist towel and baking them that way helps to retain the moisture in the biscuit. You can also microwave Pillsbury Southern Style Biscuits. To heat in the microwave, put a single biscuit on a microwavable plate and heat for 20 seconds. Let it stand for a few minutes before consuming. Are These Biscuits Good for Biscuits and Gravy? The Pillsbury biscuit recipe is the perfect complement to your favorite biscuits and gravy dish. They are not pre-sliced, but you can easily pull them open to pour sausage gravy over the top for a warm breakfast. Are There Any Allergen Considerations for Southern Style Biscuits? Those with milk and wheat sensitivities should know these are the main ingredients. However, they are certified kosher for those following a kosher diet.

introduction: Tackle your toughest cleaning jobs with Scotch-Brite® Heavy Duty Scour Pads (20ct.). From dishes to grills, garden tools and more, these scour pads help you clean every room of your home. Discover Scotch-Brite Pads Scotch-Brite Heavy Duty Scour Pads feature tough, synthetic fibers. These abrasive fibers are heat-set to retain their open design, which helps improve durability when scrubbing. The resin content helps the fibers resist breaking down when using with hot water, cleaning liquids and detergents for a durable pad that lasts through multiple cleaning jobs. What Can I Clean with Scotch-Brite Pads? Scotch-Brite Heavy Duty Scour Pads are designed for tough messes. Use them to clean burned-on foods from cast-iron pots and stove burners. Pair them with baking soda and vinegar to remove grime in the oven. Remove hard water spots from bathtubs, sinks and shower doors. Scotch-Brite pads help you remove dirt and soil from garden tools and pots. Keep one in the garage to remove grease and dirt from tools, outdoor furniture and grills. Are Scotch-Brite Pads Non-Scratch? Green Scotch-Brite scouring pads are for heavy-duty cleaning. The pads feature aggressive fibers that are not recommended for cleaning polished surfaces or those that scratch easily. Dry pads provide stronger cleaning, while wetting the fibers with water helps soften them. Always test the scouring pad on an inconspicuous spot if you are unsure if the surface is easy to scratch. Reusable Scotch-Brite Pads These pads offer durable cleaning that typically lasts through multiple jobs. Rinse the sponge completely with water to remove cleansers and detergents. Soak the scrub sponge in a cleaning solution to remove grease, dirt and heavy soil. Rinse with water and allow the pad to dry before storing so it's ready for use when needed. While some serious cleaning jobs may result in the need for multiple scrub pads, the overall durability generally provides multiple uses.

Prep Time: 20 minutes / Total Time: 1 hour, 30 minutes / Serves: 8 Ingredients 8 medium Russet potatoes 4 strips bacon, cooked and crumbled 3 finely chopped scallions 2 1/2 cups shredded cheddar cheese 2 tablespoons unsalted butter 1 cup Daisy Sour Cream 1/4 cup heavy cream 1/2 cup whole milk Pinch salt, pepper, and chili powder Directions 1. Preheat oven 400°F. Wash and dry potatoes. Wrap in aluminum foil and bake 30 minutes. 2. Remove from oven. Poke holes in potatoes and bake for another 30 minutes or until easily pierced with fork. 3. introduction: Member’s Mark™ Fresh Young Chicken features all of what you want—and nothing you don’t. Like all-natural, wholesome chicken from flocks raised and processed in the U.S.A. with no antibiotics ever and fed a vegetarian diet (no animal byproducts!). With no preservatives or additives, the superior flavor of fresh, clean, nutritious whole chicken is the centerpiece of any meal for special occasions or every day. With enough servings to feed a family of 4 per whole chicken, it’s easy and convenient to add 1-2 more chickens per roasting pan to size-up for a larger crowd, or meal prep for the week with plenty of leftovers. Simple Roasted Chicken Heat oven to 450 degrees. Prepare chicken by rubbing 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil over the entire chicken. Simply season with sea salt, black pepper, or your favorite poultry seasoning to taste. Stuff whole chicken with celery and onion for added flavor – or bread cube stuffing—if desired. Add a ½ cup chicken stock or cooking wine, and ¼ cup butter (cut into cubes) to roasting pan. Cover loosely with foil (tented), or with roasting pan cover. Roast at 450 degrees for 10 minutes, and then reduce oven heat to 350 degrees. Unpack your flowers immediately upon arrival. Fill a clean container/vase with fresh, cool water. Pro Tips & Tricks: How to Care for Your Bouquets Always start with a clean vase or display bucket. Add flower food and tap water; approximately 1-2 inches of water is sufficient. Use clipper provided to carefully cut the plastic straps that hold the bouquets to the shipping box. Paper wrap should be removed to inspect bouquet upon arrival; if there are any minor signs of bruising on the outer petals, they can be removed carefully before the event. Remove hydration sponge and bag from the lower stems. Cut at an angle, about ½"-1" off the bottom of the stem with flower clipper provided. Place in 1-2 inches of water making sure only the stems are in the water without getting the ribbon wet. Place stems in a vase or bucket immediately after cutting to ensure proper hydration. Place flower in a cool location out of sunlight and away from heat sources. To maintain bloom developments and keep flowers from opening further, keep in refrigeration at about 34-36°F. Leaving flowers at room temperature will promote natural development of bloom and will help blooms open beyond the stage at with they arrive. Avoid touching flowers; touching the petals may cause bruising that is not immediately visible but can appear as browning or wrinkles. Avoid laying bouquets sideways on flat surfaces as this may damage the outer blooms. Keep bouquets in water until the last possible moment to keep flowers fresh and hydrated. Do not expose the flowers to heat at any time before the function (do not leave outdoors, in a car, etc.). Pro Tips & Tricks: How to Make Your Flowers Last Longer Before your flowers ship, they are prepared for their journey with proper hydration methods. If your flowers appear sleepy and thirsty after their journey, this is absolutely normal! Just follow these simple steps for proper rehydration and watch them bloom to their fullest potential. Unpack your flowers immediately upon arrival. Fill a clean container/vase with fresh, cool water. Using sharp scissors or garden shears, make a 45-degree angle cut at least 1-2 inches off the end of the stems. Place the flowers in the prepared container or vase. Arrange as desired. Allow your flowers to properly hydrate for 1-2 hours. Remove any foliage that falls below the waterline of your container. Leaves will rot and cause bacteria to form and shorten the flower's life. Re-cut the stems and refresh the flower food and water every two days. Do not place flowers in direct sunlight or near fruits, heat and drafts. Remove wilting flowers at any time to prevent bacterial growth. Check out our Floral Care Guide for seasonal stems and other floral beauties. Need to Know!
